title: You are the form of light
word: You are the form of light
hook: man too jot saroop hai: O mind, you are the form of light; know your origin (Asa M3, ang 441)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the old Guru's voice: Guru Amar Das, patient with a wandering mind, saying ego and the Name won't fit in one place.

Man too jot saroop hai. A short run of Punjabi that lands like a hand on the shoulder. Guru Amar Das has been talking to the mind like someone who keeps drifting off. Here he stops calling it home for a moment and tells it what it is. Not a problem to fix. Not a list of failures. A form of light. The line is in Raga Asa, on Ang four hundred forty-one of the Guru Granth Sahib, and it opens by speaking to the mind directly: man too. O mind, you.
screen: `MAN TOO JOT SAROOP HAI.` → `NOT A PROBLEM TO FIX.` → `O MIND, YOU.`

segments.voice: Here's the line, paraphrased: O my mind, you are the very form of light; recognize your own origin. Jot is light, the same word Sikhs use for the light that passed from Guru to Guru. Saroop is form, likeness. Mool is root, origin, where something starts. So the line holds a picture and an instruction. The picture: underneath the noise, you are light. The instruction: go find where it came from. The hymn goes on, again paraphrased: O mind, the Lord is with you; through the Guru's teaching, enjoy that love. Recognize your origin and you'll know your Lord, and understand dying and living. Notice the order. It doesn't say you are the Lord, so stop looking. It says you are light, so look for the source of the light. Knowing yourself and knowing your Lord turn out to be one road. That fits the week behind us. Guru Angad called the Guru a light in the darkness, warned that service can carry pride, and called ego an illness with its cure inside. Guru Amar Das said ego and the Name can't share a room. And now, the reason the room is worth clearing: what lives there is light. Some readers hear this line as the quiet center of all the warnings. They aren't there because the mind is worthless. They're there because it's made of something precious, and keeps forgetting.
screen: `JOT, SAROOP, MOOL.` · `LIGHT, FORM, ORIGIN.` · `KNOW YOUR ROOT, KNOW YOUR LORD.` · `WHY THE WARNINGS MATTER.` · then, large: `YOU ARE LIGHT.`

segments.voice: Let the words ride the breath: in, man too jot saroop hai; out, know your origin. You don't have to work out what it means, only turn toward where your life came from and stay there gently, and if a harsh thought about yourself shows up, set it beside the line and let the line be louder. If you pray, Waheguru can take the out-breath instead.
You are the form of light. Man too jot saroop hai: O mind, you are the form of light; recognize your origin. Today's word.
screen: `YOU ARE THE FORM OF LIGHT — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: you are light. That closes this week, from Guru Angad's few lines to Guru Amar Das's call to the mind. Back tomorrow, same hill.

howItsDone: This line of Guru Amar Das from Raga Asa is often sung in kirtan and quoted in katha at the gurdwara; some Sikhs keep it as a reminder when they recite or reflect on their own.

chat.says: Guru Amar Das warns about ego so much. Does he think the mind is worthless?
options: No. He calls the mind a form of light; the warnings matter because it keeps forgetting.
Yes. He says the mind is dark at its root and must be replaced by the Word.
No. He says the mind is light already, so the warnings about ego can be ignored.
chat.meaning: Man too jot saroop hai: O mind, you are the form of light. The warnings about ego matter because the mind is precious and keeps forgetting.
